major_concerns: Accurate vendor DSL grammars are hard to construct and may be incomplete—coverage bias can skew syntactic-failure measurements.
Grammar enforcement can mask semantic/regression errors (passes syntax but fails behavior).
Public vendor samples may not represent production complexity (external validity concern).
Constrained-decoding implementations differ across APIs; engineering portability risk.
required_design_repairs: Provide explicit grammar-coverage metrics and methods for measuring grammar completeness per vendor.
Publish/share the exact grammars, parser versions, and grammar-construction protocol in artifacts to enable replication.
Include a semantic-regression test suite that runs on samples that pass parsing to quantify hidden semantic errors.
Specify constrained-decoding implementation details (API/algorithm, sampling interactions) and measure latency/compute overheads per arm.
Preregister per-vendor sampling quotas and a plan for tasks excluded due to unconstructible grammars (report exclusions).

major_concerns: Verifier coverage/fidelity may confound attribution (improvement might reflect verifier detection rather than better generation).
Emulator fidelity may not capture production regressions leading to optimistic results.
Latency/cost tradeoffs may make the G→V→R approach impractical for some operational SLAs.
Potential selection bias in chosen change‑intent benchmark (easy vs edge cases).
required_design_repairs: Preregister and publish the verifier specification, rule/feature coverage matrix, and test-cases used to validate emulator fidelity.
Add ablation arms: (a) verifier-only (blocker) and (b) repair-without-verifier feedback to disentangle effects.
Include explicit latency and compute-cost measurement and report cost-per-successful-apply.
Provide sample-size/power calculation and stopping rules tied to the preregistered primary outcome.
Describe emulator validation: map emulator test failures to known production-failure classes or cite prior emulator validation work.

major_concerns: Adversarial corpus representativeness: curated attacks may not cover real-world adaptive attackers (overfitting risk).
Ethical and safety handling of harmful prompts/configs is required—storage and sharing constraints may impede reproducibility.
Defenses may trade reduced attack success for high false-positive rates harming operator throughput and trust.
Operational cost/latency of ensembles and independent judges may render top-performing defenses impractical.
required_design_repairs: Preregister detailed ethical safeguards (IRB/ethics review, storage/encryption, access controls) and a safe-handling protocol for harmful artifacts.
Publish the adversarial corpus selection methodology and provide a version that redacts actionable payloads or provide a synthetic reproducible generator for attacks.
Include baseline defenses and ablations (e.g., single verifier vs ensemble vs judge) to attribute gains and costs.
Measure and preregister false-positive impact on benign tasks and operator-review overhead; report latency and resource costs.
Specify how ensemble diversity is constructed and validate that verifiers are independent with different failure modes.

major_concerns: Incompatible with the declared capability manifest: human_scientific_labour_allowed is false—planned human-subject recruitment and IRB procedures cannot be executed under the run constraints.
Human-subject variability and IRB limits threaten reproducibility and timeline feasibility.
Simulated tasks may not reflect real operator fatigue/workload despite counterbalancing (external validity).
Ethical risks exposing participants to adversarial/harmful suggestions require substantial mitigation and oversight.
required_design_repairs: Cannot proceed under current run constraints. Either (A) remove human-subject component and replace with validated operator-behavior simulators or historic operator decision logs (public) to emulate supervision, or (B) postpone until human-subject work is permitted and IRB/consent processes are in place.
If converted to simulation, preregister the operator-model construction, validation against real operator logs (if available), and the process for mapping model outputs to accept/reject actions.
If human subjects become permitted, preregister sample-size/power, recruitment criteria, IRB approvals, and detailed debriefing/mitigation procedures.
